din604.source: DIN 604 flat countersunk nib bolt (Senkschraube mit Nase), M12: head diameter dk=24.65 (tabulated 23.35-24.65) and head height k=7.0 (max), nib width nib_w=3.6 (g, tabulated 3.12-3.6), confirmed by fasteners.eu DIN 604 table + Fuller Fasteners DIN 604 specifications + boltingspecialist.com DIN 604 (all M12 dk-max 24.65, g-max 3.6, head-angle 90-95 deg). nib_d=5.7 is the tabulated M12 'i' minimum, read as the RADIAL nose height above the shank (the figure's i arrow is radial, same reading as DIN 607; the legacy raster confirms: back face starts ~5.3 mm above the shank). The nib is drawn as a wedge alongside the head cone per the DIN 604 figure, with two corners on existing silhouette vertices (matching the legacy raster): the top corner is the head-rim corner (dk/2, k) and the back face lands exactly on the cone-shank junction; the nose corner sits at (d_shank/2 + i, i*tan(15deg)) -- back face 15 deg from the radial per the figure, and the outer edge's ~5-deg taper emerges from the tabulated numbers. d_shank=12.0 (M12 major, envelope-only, no drawn thread); length=50.0 REPRESENTATIVE (DIN 604 lists lengths 20-160); tip_chamfer=1.2 REPRESENTATIVE 45-degree lead. Envelope only - no thread, no drive (the nib is the anti-rotation feature).

din604d.source: DIN 604 M12, app image-variant key - identical flat countersunk nib-bolt envelope (dk=24.65, k=7, nib g=3.6/i=5.7); aliases the din604 base.

din607.source: DIN 607 cup (round) head nib bolt (Flachrundschraube mit Nase), M12: head diameter dk=24.65 (tabulated 23.35-24.65) and head height k=9.65 (tabulated 8.75-9.65), nib width nib_w=3.6 (g, tabulated 3.12-3.6), confirmed by Fuller Fasteners DIN 607 specifications (M12: dk 23.35-24.65, k 8.75-9.65, g 3.12-3.6, i min 3.2, head radius r approx 13.3) + fasten.it DIN 607 table (M12: dk-max 24.65, k 8.75-9.65, g-max 3.6, i-min 3.2; grade C, sizes M8-M16). The dome is drawn as the spherical cap through dk/k (the tabulated r approx 13.3 matches the derived cap radius 12.7 within its 'approx' tolerance). The nib is a triangular wedge on the shank hugging the bearing face, per the DIN 607 figure: the tabulated i=3.2 is read as the RADIAL nose height above the shank (the figure's i arrow is radial, and the legacy raster shows ~3 mm protrusion with the figure's 30-degree underside slope), so nib_l=9.2 = d_shank/2 + i; nib_d=5.5 REPRESENTATIVE is the wedge's axial extent from that slope (i/tan(30deg) = 5.54). d_shank=12.0 (M12 major, envelope-only, no drawn thread); length=50.0 REPRESENTATIVE stock length; tip_chamfer=1.2 REPRESENTATIVE 45-degree lead. Envelope only - no thread, no drive (the nib is the anti-rotation feature).

din607d.source: DIN 607 M12, app image-variant key - identical cup-head nib-bolt envelope (dk=24.65, k=9.65, nib g=3.6/i=3.2); aliases the din607 base.
